brief.scope: Work order: the uncited-correction gate. The requirements are the ten numbered Contract items of .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md, tracked in this snapshot at the ref; read it and .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-discipline.md WHOLE from the snapshot tree. Nothing else is a requirement. Refuse at mint any write job that answers reviewer findings unless every finding it answers is named by key, disposed in the findings ledger, and the disposition cites the numbered contract item it violates; the ladder stops before its fix stages instead of correcting. No override. Boundaries as listed there; do not widen them.

findings.claim: Contract items 1, 2, 6, and 8: accepted answer keys are never tied to the review records that classify the dispatch as a correction. A previously disposed, cited key from an unrelated review can therefore stand in for the new review, creating a no-override escape and a false audit trail.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'import importlib.util,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path("ops/conductor/tools/correction.py"); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("c",p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); review="20260901T000000Z-review-grok-aaaaaa"; other="20260902T000000Z-review-grok-bbbbbb#1"; m._read_record=lambda rid,records: {"id":rid,"job":"adversarial-review"}; m._scope_path=lambda inputs,root: ".dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md"; m._answer_row=lambda key,*args: {"key":key}; r=m.check("write",[review],[],[other],"2099-01-01T00:00:00Z","records","jobs","."); print(r); assert r["correction"] and r["answers"][0]["key"]==other'

findings.claim: Contract items 3 and 4: every refusal remedy hard-codes disposition `fixed` and `contract item 1` without reading the finding's claim or cited item. Following the prescribed command for a finding that violates another item writes false evidence which the gate accepts, defeating the required finding-to-contract disposition.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'import importlib.util,inspect,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path("ops/conductor/tools/correction.py"); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("c",p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); cmd=m._disposition_command("20260901T000000Z-review-grok-aaaaaa#1",".dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md"); print(cmd); assert " fixed " in cmd and "contract item 1 of" in cmd and "claim" not in inspect.getsource(m._answer_row)'

findings.claim: Contract item 4: when a brief names both the work-order scope and `scope-discipline.md`, the first `scope-*` input silently wins. Reordering those normal inputs makes a discipline-clause item satisfy the gate even though only the ten work-order Contract items are requirements, widening the correction boundary instead of refusing ambiguity.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'import importlib.util,pathlib; p=pathlib.Path("ops/conductor/tools/correction.py"); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("c",p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); root=pathlib.Path.cwd(); selected=m._scope_path([".dev/ladder-inputs/scope-discipline.md",".dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md"],root); ok,reason=m.FINDINGS.citation_holds(f"contract item 1 of {selected}: bypass",root,selected); print(selected,ok,reason); assert selected==".dev/ladder-inputs/scope-discipline.md" and ok'

findings.claim: Contract item 9: `cited` interpolates the ledger row's `record` directly into a filesystem path without validating the record ID or containing the resolved path. A crafted tracked record or symlink can make the conductor read JSON outside the repository. This requires hostile tracked state, so it is P3 under D-LAUNCHER-1.
findings.reproduce: python3 -B -c 'import importlib.util,inspect,pathlib; from unittest.mock import patch; p=pathlib.Path("ops/conductor/tools/findings.py"); s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("f",p); m=importlib.util.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); seen=[]; q=patch.object(pathlib.Path,"read_text",lambda self,*a,**k: seen.append(self) or "{\"brief\":{\"inputs\":[]}}"); q.start(); m._record_scope("/etc/agentscient-probe"); q.stop(); escaped=seen[0].resolve(); print(escaped); assert escaped==pathlib.Path("/etc/agentscient-probe.json") and not escaped.is_relative_to(m.RECORDS.resolve()) and ".resolve" not in inspect.getsource(m._record_scope)'

envelope.note: Read all three in/ inputs and both tracked scope documents whole. Covered argv/shell, SQL/template, secrets, path/ref containment, permission/sandbox records, vendor-output trust, and supply-chain surfaces. The repository secret scanner was clean on all 13 changed tracked files; SQL is parameterized; no dependency, lockfile, fetched-action, ref, credential, or sandbox-flag defect was found. Stateful unittest suites could not run because the audit sandbox exposes no writable temporary directory; non-mutating reproductions, Ruff without cache, diff checking, and JSON parsing ran successfully. The findings store was not read.
